Long Page

Fastrag is a small toolkit for building retrieval-augmented chatbots out of dynamic sources. This fixture page exists purely to carry enough prose that splitting it at a small chunk size produces more than one chunk, which is the one thing a chunking test genuinely needs from its input text.

A pipeline in this package is built from lazy steps: fetchers turn a location into raw bytes, parsers turn those bytes into text, chunkers split that text into smaller pieces, embedders attach a vector to each piece, and a vector store persists the result. None of this work happens until the graph is actually evaluated.

Caching is explicit and per step rather than a hidden global behind the scenes. A step handed a cache backend consults it before doing any real work, and writes back whatever it produced once it is done, so a second run of the same pipeline against the same configuration can skip everything it already has an answer for.

Every step emits events as it runs: one when it starts, one for every item it produces, one when it finishes, and one if it fails outright. A logger or any other consumer can subscribe to this stream without the step itself knowing or caring who, if anyone, is listening.

None of this paragraph's content matters beyond its length: it is here only to push the total size of this page well past what a chunk size of a few dozen characters could hold in one piece, so a splitter run against it is forced to produce several chunks rather than just one.
